OKX and NYSE Parent ICE Launch Tokenized Stock Venue With 113 Assets Lined Up
sum: Eligible U.S. customers of OKX will be able to buy tokenized shares through OKXICE, the venture crypto exchange OKX formed with Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), owner of the New York Stock Exchange, when its venue goes live at 12 p.m. ET Monday, the company said. The venture announced the launch earlier Monday, saying the venue will appear as a new tab in the OKX app and that 113 stocks, ETFs and exchange-traded products (ETPs) are slated to be added in stages from Nov. 23.

That is up from the more than 70 assets the venture named when it set the date on Nov. 11. The new names are eToro, Fidelity Investments, Strive and Vida Global, which join Better.com, BitGo, Circle, Coinbase, Direxion, Robinhood, Securitize and Strategy. The venue’s public notice dated Nov. 20 lists six stocks available at launch, each paired with the USDC stablecoin: Coinbase, Securitize, Strategy, BitGo, Robinhood and Circle.
The same notice names 67 companies that objected to tokenized versions of their shares trading there, including Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla. The tally is unchanged from the Nov. 5 notice.

Only vetted users get in. Buyers must be eligible U.S. customers of OKX Inc. who pass identity checks, and the venue’s smart contracts block any wallet that hasn’t been approved from trading or supplying liquidity. Those wallets stay in the customer’s own custody. Securitize, which trades on the NYSE as SECZ, tokenizes the shares; each token, the announcement said, is backed by one real share and passes through dividends and voting rights. Trades settle against automated market maker (AMM) pools built with Uniswap v4 on X Layer, OKX’s own Ethereum layer-2 network.

The notice says pool prices are set by each pool’s asset ratio, not the underlying stock’s market, so they can drift, especially after hours. The venue runs under the SEC’s Innovation Exemption, temporary conditional relief the agency issued in September. The exemption lets qualifying venues trade tokenized versions of U.S.-listed stocks if they meet conditions such as limits on trading volume.

Traders can keep a position as long as they keep enough margin posted, and a periodic funding payment between long and short owners keeps the contract's price anchored to the underlying asset. sum: Major listed companies are mounting a collective pushback against the stock tokenization project pursued by OKXICE, a joint venture between Intercontinental Exchange (ICE)—the parent of the New York Stock Exchange—and crypto exchange OKX. According to an OKXICE notice published on the 3rd (local time), 56 of the 62 target companies have filed objections. Among them, six companies—Tesla, Amazon, SpaceX, Netflix, Lam Research and SoFi Technologies—newly expressed their opposition in this round.

In particular, five of the six Magnificent Seven (M7) members other than Apple have joined the opposition: Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Tesla. Apple is the only M7 company that has not objected. Broadcom, Qualcomm, Oracle, Intel, Micron, AMD, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Wells Fargo, McDonald's, Coca-Cola, Walmart and Eli Lilly also appear on the objection list.

The objections are grounded in an innovation exemption issued by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in September. The exemption allows exchanges such as OKXICE to handle tokenized U.S. stocks without registering as formal exchanges, while also granting companies the right to object to third-party tokenization of their shares. OKXICE issued its first notice on the 4th of last month, after which a 30-day objection window was granted; that deadline fell on this day.

Stock tokenization is a method of representing assets or rights linked to physical shares as blockchain-based digital tokens. It has drawn interest from the global financial industry because it enables fractional trading and 24-hour trading. However, a key point of contention is that token holders do not receive shareholder rights such as ownership or voting rights guaranteed by the underlying shares.

The companies that newly objected did not disclose specific reasons. Industry observers, however, see the backdrop as the difficulty issuers face in tracking shareholder composition or the channels for delivering voting rights and dividends when third parties tokenize their shares without consent.

Intercontinental Exchange NYSE:ICE has launched the first exchange-traded base oils futures contracts, using pricing benchmarks from ICIS, in a move that promises to bring formal risk management tools to a corner of the oil market that has until now operated almost entirely on a physical basis.

Base oils, namely refined petroleum products used to make lubricants, sit in an awkward middle ground between crude oil and finished products. Prices are influenced by crude and feedstock costs, but also by regional supply constraints, plant outages and seasonal demand.

Despite this volatility, the market has lacked standardised financial instruments, leaving refiners, traders and end-users exposed to price swings they could manage only through physical inventory or long-term supply contracts.

The new ICE–ICIS contracts aim to change that. Cash-settled against independent ICIS price indexes, the futures provide a regulated benchmark for hedging and price discovery across three of the most important regional markets: Northwest Europe, Asia and the US Gulf coast. The initial suite focuses on Group II base oils, widely used in automotive and industrial lubricants, and includes N150 FCA Northwest Europe, N150 FOB Asia and N100/120 FOB US Gulf export contracts.

items.t: Exchange-backed base oils futures
sum: A new suite of exchange-backed base oils futures contracts using ICIS benchmarks is set to bring risk management tools to a market that has, until now, traded almost exclusively on a physical basis.

London, 13 January 2026 – Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), a leading global provider of technology and data, in collaboration with ICIS, a global leader in commodity intelligence, has launched the first exchange-backed futures contracts for base oils. Using ICIS pricing benchmarks, the new contracts represent a significant step forward in the management of price risk in the global base oils market. Cash-settled against independent ICIS base oils price indexes, the contracts provide refiners, traders, distributors and end-users with a robust reference for hedging and price discovery across Europe, Asia and the US.

Until now, base oils have largely been traded on a purely physical basis, leaving participants directly exposed to price swings driven by crude oil, feedstocks, regional imbalances and seasonality. The introduction of ICE–ICIS-linked Group II base oils futures establish a regulated, exchange-traded hedging instrument tailored to this market, enabling users to lock in forward prices, stabilise margins and separate physical supply decisions from price risk.
The ICE–ICIS-linked Group II base oils futures suite covers three key regional benchmarks on FCA (free carrier) and FOB (free on board) terms, creating a global risk management framework:

Together, these instruments enable market participants to hedge exposure across major producing and consuming hubs using a single, consistent set of benchmarks and contract structures.
